Open to New Opportunities 🚀
Being unemployed isn’t easy. It can come with uncertainty, self-doubt, and many questions about what comes next. But I’m choosing to view this chapter not as a setback, but as an opportunity to learn, grow, and find the right next step.
I’m currently open to new opportunities and would be grateful to connect with individuals, teams, and organizations looking for someone who is committed, adaptable, and eager to make a meaningful contribution.
I’m particularly interested in opportunities where I can:
• Contribute meaningfully and help solve real-world problems
• Learn from talented people and gain new perspectives
• Grow professionally while taking on meaningful challenges
• Bring commitment, adaptability, and a strong willingness to learn
If you know of a suitable opportunity, project, organization, or hiring team—or if you can offer advice, an introduction, or a lead—I would genuinely appreciate hearing from you.
Sometimes, the right opportunity starts with a simple connection. 🤝
Thank you to everyone who reaches out, shares this post, makes an introduction, or simply keeps me in mind. Your support can make a real difference. 🙏

Great conversations, great people, and great coffee ☕💻

Had an amazing time at the Devin Kampala Meetup at Inspire Café! 🇺🇬

It was a great opportunity to connect with fellow developers, exchange ideas, learn more about AI-powered development, and discuss how tools like Devin are shaping the future of software engineering.

Beyond the technology, the meetup was about community, collaboration, and learning from one another. Meeting passionate builders and sharing experiences made the event truly worthwhile.

A big thank you to everyone who made the meetup happen and to all the developers who showed up, contributed, asked questions, and shared their perspectives. 🙌

Here’s to more meetups, more learning, and more building together! 🚀

One of the goals I had when building StreetJS wasn't just to create another backend framework.
I wanted to build a framework that developers could extend.
A framework where integrations feel like first-class citizens instead of custom code copied from project to project.
Today, I'm excited to share one example of that vision:
🚀 StreetJS MarzPay Plugin
With this plugin, developers can integrate MarzPay into their StreetJS applications with a clean, modular experience, making it easier to build payment-enabled applications on top of the framework.
What excites me most isn't just this plugin—it's what it represents.
It proves that StreetJS isn't only a framework for building applications; it's a platform for building an ecosystem of reusable plugins that solve real-world problems.
This is just the beginning.
I hope to see developers build integrations for databases, messaging platforms, cloud providers, AI services, payment gateways, and many more technologies using StreetJS.
If you're interested in building with StreetJS or creating plugins for the ecosystem, I'd love to hear your ideas.

🚀 A huge thank you to the Kiro team.
 
Building an open-source framework from scratch is a long journey.
 
There are countless architecture decisions, documentation, testing, refactoring, and thousands of lines of code before anyone ever sees the first release.
 
Over the past months, I've been working on StreetJS, a modern TypeScript backend framework, and I'm grateful to have been part of the Kiro Startup Program.
 
Kiro became an important part of my development workflow, helping me move from ideas to implementation faster and making it easier to organize and execute complex engineering tasks. That allowed me to spend more time focusing on the architecture and developer experience I wanted StreetJS to deliver.
 
Today, StreetJS is available as an open-source project.

Here's to building more great open-source software. 🚀
